newsitem.title: CANADA: TimberWest stock up after net, sale news.
newsitem.headline: TimberWest stock up after net, sale news.

text.p: Shares in TimberWest Forest Ltd rose Friday after the lumber producer announced higher earnings and a decision to sell its privately-owned timberlands.
TimberWest stock was up 1.30 to 19.05, one of the top gainers on the Toronto exchange. Stock in Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd, 52 percent owner of TimberWest, dropped 0.15 to 22.
TimberWest announced earlier that its earnings in its second fiscal quarter to December 31 rose to C$0.61 a share including a C$0.29 tax again from C$0.16 a year earlier.
The lumber company attributed the gain to strong demand in the United States and Japan.

Fletcher Canada, majority owned by New Zealand's Fletcher Challenge Ltd, announced late Thursday that TimberWest's private forestlands would be sold on the market by way of an income fund and the proceeds distributed to shareholders.

TimberWest put itself up for sale in October and explored both a sale of the whole company and specific assets. The process took longer than investors anticipated and analysts speculated that the delay meant that offers did not live up to expectations of a deal in the range of C$21 a share.
TimberWest's directors said they believe the proceeds from the forestlands sale and the value of TimberWest stock after the sale will equal more than TimberWest's current share price.
Canfor Corp, the forest company that had been rumored as the likely buyer of TimberWest, saw its stock drop 0.10 to 13.50 heavy trading.
